title: 以前, 以后, 后来 and more time words
explain: 以前 means 'before' and 以后 means 'after'. They come after a time or a verb: 八点以前 'before eight'; 睡觉以前 'before going to bed'; 吃饭以后 'after eating'. On their own they also mean 'in the past' and 'later, in the future'.
后来 means 'afterwards' and is only used about the past: 他以前不喝咖啡，后来喝了 'He did not drink coffee before; later he did'. For the future use 以后: 以后我想去中国.
然后 means 'then, after that', the next step in a series (past or future). 最后 means 'finally, last': 最后一个问题.
More time words: 前天 'the day before yesterday', 后天 'the day after tomorrow', 前年 'the year before last', 后年 'the year after next', 最近 'recently'.

examples.en: I must arrive before eight.

examples.zh: 睡觉以前，他喜欢听音乐。
examples.en: Before going to bed, he likes listening to music.

examples.zh: 他以前不喝咖啡，后来喝了。
examples.en: He did not drink coffee before; later he did.
I saw him the day before yesterday.

mistakes: 后来 is only for the past. For the future say 以后: 以后我想去中国, not 后来我想去中国.
以前 and 以后 come after the time or verb: 八点以前, not 以前八点.

q.en: I must arrive before eight.
After eating, we go for a walk.

q.zh: 睡觉以前，他喜欢听音乐。
q.en: Before going to bed, he likes listening to music.

q.zh: 他以前不喝咖啡，后来喝了。
q.en: He did not drink coffee before; later he did.
q.explain: 后来 is for the past.

q.prompt: Which sentence says: I want to go to China in the future?
q.en: I want to go to China in the future.
q.explain: 以后 can look to the future; 后来 cannot.

title: 应该, 必须, 需要, 不用 and 最好
explain: 应该 (or 该) means 'should': 你应该多休息 'You should rest more'. The negative is 不应该.
必须 means 'must, have to': 学生必须在八点以前到学校 'Students must be at school before eight'. Do not say 不必须. The opposite of 必须 is 不用, 'no need to': 你不用急，慢慢来 'There is no need to rush; take your time'.
需要 is a verb that means 'need': 我需要你的帮助 'I need your help'. It can also be followed by a verb: 你需要多休息.
最好 means 'had better': 外面很冷，你最好多穿一点儿 'It is cold outside, so you had better wear a bit more'.

examples.en: You should rest more.

examples.zh: 学生必须在八点以前到学校。
examples.en: Students must be at school before eight.
There is no need to rush; take your time.

examples.zh: 外面很冷，你最好多穿一点儿。
examples.en: It is cold outside, so you had better wear a bit more.

mistakes: Do not say 不必须. The opposite of 必须 is 不用: 你不用来, not 你不必须来.
应该 and 该 both mean should. 该 is shorter and more common in speech.

q.en: You should rest more.
You do not need to rush.
q.explain: 不用 means no need to.

q.en: I need your help.

q.zh: 外面很冷，你最好多穿一点儿。
q.en: It is cold outside, so you had better wear a bit more.

q.prompt: Which sentence says: You must come at eight?
q.en: You must come at eight.

title: 只, 只是 and 只能: only
explain: 只 before a verb means 'only': 我只喝水 'I only drink water'; 他只会说汉语 'He can only speak Chinese'. It goes right before the verb.
只是 means 'just, merely': 我只是想帮你 'I just want to help you'; 这只是一个小问题 'This is only a small problem'.
只能 means 'can only, have no choice but to': 没有别的办法，我们只能等 'There is no other way; we can only wait'.
Do not confuse the 'only' 只 (zhǐ) with the measure word 只 (zhī) in 一只猫.

examples.en: I only drink water.
He can only speak Chinese.
I just want to help you.

examples.zh: 没有别的办法，我们只能等。
examples.en: There is no other way; we can only wait.

mistakes: 只 goes right before the verb: 我只喝水, not 我喝只水.
只有 is a different word: it needs 才 in the next part (see 只要 and 只有).

q.en: I only drink water.
He can only speak Chinese.
I just want to help you.
There are no cars, so we can only walk.

q.prompt: Which sentence says: I am just asking?
q.en: I am just asking.
q.explain: 只是 comes before the verb.

title: 好像, 看起来, 大概, 其实 and 当然
explain: 好像 means 'it seems, as if': 他好像不在家 'He does not seem to be at home'. 看起来 means 'it looks like': 这个菜看起来很好吃 'This dish looks delicious'. 看来 means 'it seems (from what I can see)': 看来明天要下雨 'It seems it will rain tomorrow'.
大概 means 'probably, roughly': 现在大概九点了 'It is probably about nine now'.
其实 means 'actually, in fact' and points out how things really are, often against what people think: 其实我不是老师 'Actually, I am not a teacher'.
当然 means 'of course': 你会游泳吗？——我当然会 'Can you swim? Of course I can'.

examples.en: He does not seem to be at home.
This dish looks delicious.
It is probably about nine now.
Actually, I am not a teacher.

mistakes: 好像 here means 'seems', not 'like'. For 'like' (be fond of) use 喜欢.
其实 points to the real situation, so it often goes against what was just said. Do not use it just to agree.

q.en: He does not seem to be at home.
q.explain: 好像 goes before the part that seems true.

q.en: This dish looks delicious.
It is probably about nine now.
Actually, I am not a teacher.

q.prompt: Which sentence says: Of course I can swim?
q.en: Of course I can swim.
q.explain: 当然 goes before the verb.

title: 终于, 几乎, 突然, 马上 and 一定
explain: 终于 means 'at last, finally' and is for something you waited for: 火车终于来了 'The train has finally come'. 几乎 means 'almost, nearly': 我几乎忘了他的名字 'I almost forgot his name'; 几乎没 means 'hardly any': 他几乎没吃东西.
突然 means 'suddenly': 突然，他笑了 'Suddenly, he laughed'; 天突然下雨了 'It suddenly started to rain'. It can go before the subject or before the verb.
马上 means 'right away': 我马上就到 'I will be there right away'. 一定 means 'certainly, must': 我一定会给你打电话 'I will definitely call you'.
All of these go right before the verb; 突然 can also start the sentence.

examples.en: The train has finally come.
I almost forgot his name.
Suddenly, he laughed.
I will definitely call you.

mistakes: Use 终于 only for a result you were waiting for. For a surprise, say 突然.
Put these words before the verb: 我马上就到, not 我到马上.

q.en: The train has finally come.
q.explain: 终于 goes before the verb.

q.en: He suddenly laughed.
q.explain: 突然 goes before the verb.

q.en: I almost forgot his name.
I will be there right away.

q.prompt: Which sentence says: I will definitely call you?
q.en: I will definitely call you.
q.explain: 一定 goes before the verb.

title: Question words for "any": 谁都, 想吃什么就吃什么, 一个也不
explain: A question word + 都 or 也 means 'every' or 'any': 谁都知道这件事 'Everyone knows about this'; 我哪儿都不想去 'I don't want to go anywhere'. With 不 or 没 it means 'nothing, nobody, nowhere': 我什么都没买 'I did not buy anything'.
想 + question word + 就 + the same question word means 'as you like': 你想吃什么就吃什么 'Eat whatever you want'; 你想去哪儿就去哪儿 'Go wherever you want'.
一 + measure word + noun + 也 or 都 + 不 or 没 + verb means 'not even one': 教室里一个人也没有 'There is not a single person in the classroom'; 我一个字也不认识 'I do not know a single character'.

examples.en: Everyone knows about this.
I did not buy anything.
Eat whatever you want.
There is not a single person in the classroom.

mistakes: Do not leave out 都 or 也: 谁知道这件事？ is a question 'Who knows?', but 谁都知道这件事 is a statement 'Everyone knows'.
In 想…就… use the same question word twice: 想吃什么就吃什么.

q.en: Everyone knows.
I do not want to eat anything.
q.explain: Question word + 都 + 不 + verb.

q.en: Eat whatever you want.
q.explain: 想…就… repeats the question word.

q.en: I do not want to go anywhere.

q.prompt: Which sentence says: There is not a single person here?
q.en: There is not a single person here.
q.explain: 一…也没有 means not even one.

title: 半, 两三个 and 以上 / 以下
explain: 半 means 'half'. After a measure word: 一个半小时 'one and a half hours'. Before a measure word: 半个小时 'half an hour'; 半年 'half a year'.
Two numbers next to each other (smaller first) mean 'about': 两三个学生 'two or three students'; 我在这里住了七八天 'I stayed here for seven or eight days'.
以上 means 'above, and over' and counts the number itself: 十八岁以上的人 'people aged eighteen and over'. 以下 means 'below, under': 五十块以下的鞋 'shoes under fifty yuan'.

examples.en: I waited for an hour and a half.
He will be here in half an hour.
There are two or three students here.
Shoes under fifty yuan are rare.

mistakes: 半 goes before the measure word in 半个小时 but after it in 一个半小时. Do not say 一半个小时.
Put the smaller number first: 两三个, not 三两个.

q.en: I waited for an hour and a half.
There are two or three students here.
q.explain: Two numbers side by side mean about.

q.en: He will arrive in half an hour.

q.zh: 十八岁以上的人可以进去。
q.en: People aged eighteen and over can go in.

q.prompt: Which sentence says: I stayed here for seven or eight days?
q.en: I stayed here for seven or eight days.

title: Words you know, with a new meaning
explain: Some words you already know come back in HSK 3 with another meaning or another sound. The character is the same; the word around it tells you which one it is.
得 děi means 'must, have to' before a verb: 我得走了 'I have to go now'; 你得多休息 'You must rest more'. It sounds different from the 得 after a verb (他跑得很快, de), and from 得 dé 'to get' (得到, 得分).
地 dì means 'ground, place': 地方 'place', 地铁 'subway', 地图 'map', 地上 'on the ground'. It is de only after an adverb (高兴地说). 过去 is also 'the past': 过去的事 'things of the past'.

还 huán means 'to give back': 还书 'return a book', 还钱 'pay back', 还给 'give back to'. 还 hái 'still, also' is the one you already know. 会 huì also means 'a meeting': 开会 'have a meeting'. 长 zhǎng means 'to grow': 长大 'grow up', 长高 'grow taller'; 长 cháng is 'long'.

examples.en: I have to go now.
I have given the book back to him.
We have a meeting tomorrow.
The child has grown up.

mistakes: Do not mix up the sounds: 我得走了 is děi (must), 他跑得很快 is de (how). The characters are the same, the sound is decided by the words around.
还 hái 'still' goes before another verb: 我还没吃 'I have not eaten yet'. 还 huán 'give back' is the verb itself: 还书 'return a book'.

q.en: I have to go now.
You must rest more.
The child has grown up.
q.explain: 长大 is zhǎngdà, to grow up.

q.en: I have given the book back to him.
q.explain: 还给 is huán gěi, give back to.

q.prompt: Which sentence says: We have a meeting tomorrow?
q.en: We have a meeting tomorrow.
q.explain: 开会 means to have a meeting.
